_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-01 15:00:08Z)**_

Here's a draft. I checked the code so it matches how search works now: the dropdown is in [DateFilter.tsx](app/scenes/Search/components/DateFilter.tsx) and offers All time, Past day, Past week, Past month and Past year. The server filters results on `updatedAt` in [PostgresSearchProvider.ts:669](plugins/search-postgres/server/PostgresSearchProvider.ts#L669).

---

## User Story
As an Outline user searching my team's knowledge base, I want to filter search results by a custom date range so that I can find documents from a specific period, such as last quarter or a project that ran two years ago, instead of only recent ones.

## User Scenario
Maya is looking for meeting notes from a project that ran from March to May 2025. She searches "sprint retro" and gets dozens of results from several years. She opens the date filter dropdown, but the options (Past day, Past week, Past month, Past year) don't cover that period. She picks a new **"Custom range…"** option, and two date inputs appear: "From" and "To." She enters 2025-03-01 and 2025-05-31. The results now show only documents last updated in that window. The dropdown label shows "Mar 1, 2025 – May 31, 2025." She copies the URL and sends it to a teammate, who sees the same filtered results.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The search date filter dropdown has a new "Custom range" option alongside the existing options.
2. Choosing "Custom range" shows a "From" date input and a "To" date input.
3. Applying a range shows only documents whose last-updated date falls within it, including both the start and end dates.
4. The user can fill in only "From" (everything on or after that date) or only "To" (everything on or before that date).
5. If "From" is later than "To," the filter is not applied and the user sees a validation message.
6. When a custom range is active, the dropdown label shows the selected dates instead of "Any time."
7. The range is saved in the URL query parameters, so refreshing the page or sharing the link keeps the filter.
8. Choosing a preset (e.g. "Past week") or "All time" clears the custom range.
9. The API accepts the new range parameters and rejects invalid dates with a 400 error, as it already does for invalid `dateFilter` values.
10. The existing preset filters keep working as before.
11. Tests cover the new API parameters, including valid ranges, open-ended ranges, and invalid input.

## Out of Scope
- Filtering by created date instead of last-updated date
- Custom date ranges on other screens that use the date filter, such as Drafts
- Time-of-day precision (whole dates only)
- Saved or named date ranges
- Relative custom ranges (e.g. "last 90 days")

## Open Questions
- Should the range filter on **last updated** (current behavior) or **created** date? Users who ask for "old documents" may mean the date a document was created.
- Which time zone defines the start and end of a day: the user's local time zone or UTC?
- Should we use the browser's native date input or an existing date picker component in Outline?
- Should Drafts get the same option later, since it shares the date filter?
- Should future dates be allowed in the "To" field, or limited to today?

---

A few tips for this template:
- **Scenario:** a named person and concrete dates make it easy to picture.
- **Acceptance criteria:** each one should be testable as [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] or fail. Edge cases (open-ended ranges, From later than To, URL saving) are where specs usually leave gaps.
- **Out of Scope:** for a "Small" issue, this section is what keeps it small. List anything the team might assume is included.
- **Open Questions:** the created vs. updated question matters most, because today's filter uses `updatedAt`, which may not be what users expect.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-01 20:46:42Z)**_

Yes. Search already has a date filter dropdown with these options, defined in [DateFilter.tsx:16-37](app/scenes/Search/components/DateFilter.tsx#L16-L37):

- All time (the default, shown as "Any time")
- Past day
- Past week
- Past month
- Past year

How it works:
- **Frontend:** the selected option goes into the URL as `?dateFilter=day`, `week`, `month` or `year` ([Search.tsx:70](app/scenes/Search/Search.tsx#L70)).
- **Backend:** the server keeps only documents with `updatedAt > now() - interval '1 <value>'` ([PostgresSearchProvider.ts:669-677](plugins/search-postgres/server/PostgresSearchProvider.ts#L669-L677)). So "Past week" means "edited in the last 7 days," not "created in the last 7 days."
- **Validation:** the API only accepts those preset values and rejects anything else ([schema.ts:40](server/routes/api/documents/schema.ts#L40)).
- **Drafts** reuses the same component ([Drafts.tsx:28](app/scenes/Drafts.tsx#L28)).

That's why the issue says it "only supports a recent window." Every option counts back from now, so you can't pick a period in the past, like March to May 2025, or "anything before 2024." Your feature adds a "Custom range" option next to these presets rather than replacing them. That's why the spec includes the criterion that the existing preset filters keep working as before.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-06 23:58:15Z)**_

The work splits into three choices: how the API takes the range, what the user sees, and how dates are sent to the server. Here's what I found in the code first:

- The API only accepts `"day" | "week" | "month" | "year"` for the date filter ([schema.ts:39-49](server/routes/api/documents/schema.ts#L39-L49), [shared/types.ts:16](shared/types.ts#L16)).
- The server applies the filter in three places: `searchForUser` and `searchTitlesForUser` in [PostgresSearchProvider.ts](plugins/search-postgres/server/PostgresSearchProvider.ts#L669), and `documents.drafts` ([documents.ts:547](server/routes/api/documents/documents.ts#L547)).
- The browser filters loaded documents again in [DocumentsStore.ts:231](app/stores/DocumentsStore.ts#L231).
- The app already uses `react-day-picker` (v8) for [ExpiryDatePicker.tsx](app/scenes/ApiKeyNew/components/ExpiryDatePicker.tsx).

## 1. API shape

**A. Add separate `dateFrom` / `dateTo` parameters next to `dateFilter`**
- ✅ Doesn't change how existing requests behave, so current API users aren't affected
- ✅ Easy to validate with zod, e.g. `z.iso.datetime().optional()`
- ✅ Either end can be left open ("before 2024", "after March")
- ❌ There are now two ways to filter by date, so you need a rule for when both are sent (reject the request, or let one win)

**B. Make `dateFilter` also accept a range string, e.g. `"2025-03-01..2025-05-31"`**
- ✅ Still one parameter, and the URL stays short
- ❌ The typed list of allowed values becomes a free-form string you have to parse
- ❌ Harder for API users to discover and harder to validate cleanly

**C. Replace `dateFilter` with `{ from, to }` and have the browser turn presets into dates**
- ✅ The server has only one way to filter, which keeps its code simpler
- ❌ Breaking change for anyone using the public API today
- ❌ A shared "Past week" link would contain fixed dates, so it would stop meaning "the last 7 days" a few days later

## 2. Date input

**A. The browser's built-in `<input type="date">`**
- ✅ No new code to pull in, accessible, works well on mobile, quick to build
- ❌ Looks different in each browser and is hard to style to match Outline

**B. `react-day-picker` with range mode**
- ✅ Already a dependency and already used in the app, so it fits the existing look
- ✅ Range selection is built in (click a start date, then an end date)
- ❌ More work: popover placement, keyboard focus, and fitting it inside the dropdown

## 3. Time zones and the end date

**A. Send plain dates (`2025-05-31`) and let the server read them as UTC**
- ✅ Simple, and the URLs are easy to read
- ❌ Results can be off by several hours for users far from UTC

**B. The browser converts the dates to the start and end of the user's local day and sends full timestamps**
- ✅ Matches what the user expects
- ❌ Two people sharing a link from different time zones may see slightly different results

Either way, include the whole end date: compare `updatedAt < to + 1 day` (or `<= 23:59:59.999` of that day), not `<= to`. Otherwise documents edited on the end date get dropped.

## My recommendation

Use **1A + 2B + 3B**:
- It's the smallest change that doesn't break existing behavior, which fits a "Small" issue.
- It reuses a date picker the app already has.
- It gets the date boundaries right for users.

Two implementation notes:
- **Use bound values:** in the Postgres provider, build the new conditions as `{ updatedAt: { [Op.gte]: from, [Op.lt]: to } }` with the dates [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]ed as values, not with `sequelize.literal`. The existing preset is safe only because zod limits it to four values. Range dates come straight from the user, so they should never be pasted into SQL text.
- **Validate the order:** add a zod `.refine()` that rejects a request when `dateFrom > dateTo`.

These choices settle some of the spec's open questions. If you go with 1A, add an acceptance criterion for what happens when a request sends both `dateFilter` and `dateFrom`/`dateTo`.

What makes the range wide:
- **The date picker is the biggest uncertainty.** [ExpiryDatePicker.tsx](app/scenes/ApiKeyNew/components/ExpiryDatePicker.tsx) is a reference at 68 lines. The hard part is fitting a picker inside the existing [FilterOptions](app/components/FilterOptions.tsx) dropdown, which is built for a simple list of options. There are four realistic ways to build it. The good news is that Outline already has most of the parts:

- **[shared/components/Calendar.tsx](shared/components/Calendar.tsx)** is a themed wrapper around `react-day-picker`'s `DayPicker`. It accepts all of `DayPicker`'s props, including `mode="range"`.
- **`~/components/primitives/Popover`** is the popover used by [ExpiryDatePicker.tsx](app/scenes/ApiKeyNew/components/ExpiryDatePicker.tsx): a button that opens a calendar.
- **[FilterOptions.tsx](app/components/FilterOptions.tsx)** is the current dropdown. It's a menu (a Drawer on mobile) that **closes as soon as an item is clicked**. It also builds its label by finding the selected key in `options`. Both behaviors affect how a custom range can fit in.

## Option 1: Built-in browser date inputs
Choosing "Custom range" shows two `<input type="date">` fields (From and To) and an Apply button, either below the filter bar or in a small popover.

- ✅ Least code (about 30–40 lines), no calendar to style, accessible, and good on mobile (the phone's own date picker)
- ✅ Typing a date is quick for far-off ranges ("2019-01-01")
- ❌ Looks different in Chrome, Safari and Firefox and won't match Outline's styling
- ❌ The format shown depends on the browser's language, not the user's Outline language setting

## Option 2: One calendar in range mode, in a popover (recommended)
Choosing "Custom range" closes the menu and opens a popover with `<Calendar mode="range" />`. The user clicks a start day and then an end day, and the range is highlighted. The dropdown label then reads "Mar 1 – May 31, 2025."

- ✅ Reuses `Calendar` and `Popover` with the same pattern as `ExpiryDatePicker`, so it matches the rest of the app
- ✅ Choosing the range is one interaction, and the user can see the whole span
- ✅ `react-day-picker` handles keyboard navigation, the user's language and blocked dates (e.g. `disabled={{ after: new Date() }}`)
- ❌ Clicking through months to reach a date years ago is slow. Showing month and year dropdowns (`captionLayout="dropdown"` in v8) fixes this
- ❌ Needs a little plumbing: open the popover after the menu closes, and [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] a dynamic label to `FilterOptions`, e.g. by adding a `custom` option whose label is the formatted dates
- ❌ No obvious way to leave one end open. You'd need "clear" buttons or a rule that a single clicked day means "from this date on"

## Option 3: Separate From and To buttons, each opening a single-date calendar
When a custom range is active, two buttons appear in the filter bar. Each works like `ExpiryDatePicker`: click it and pick one date.

- ✅ Leaving one end open is natural: just leave "To" empty
- ✅ Very close to existing code, so `ExpiryDatePicker` can be copied almost directly
- ❌ Two popovers and two clicks, and the user never sees the whole range at once
- ❌ The user can choose From after To, so it needs its own validation, e.g. greying out invalid days in the second calendar
- ❌ Takes up more room in the filter bar, which is already crowded on mobile

## Option 4: Replace the dropdown with a combined panel (presets plus calendar)
Like Google Analytics or Linear: one popover with the presets (Past day, Past week…) listed on the left and a range calendar on the right.

- ✅ The most polished experience, with presets and custom ranges in one place
- ❌ Replaces `FilterOptions` for this filter, so you have to rebuild the mobile Drawer and keyboard behavior yourself
- ❌ Much more code (likely 150+ lines on the frontend) and more design decisions, which goes beyond a "Small" issue

## Recommendation
Go with **Option 2**, with month and year dropdowns turned on so older documents are easy to reach. It fits the "Small" scope, reuses parts the app already has, and the result looks native to Outline. For open ends, add a "Clear" link under each end of the range, or treat a range with only a start date as "from this date to now."

If fitting it into `FilterOptions` gets messy, fall back to **Option 1**. It's acceptable for a first version and is easy to replace later.

You can put the choice in your spec's Open Questions, or decide now and add matching criteria. For example: "Selecting Custom range opens a calendar where the user picks a start and end date," and "Month and year can be changed without clicking through each month."

```text
    const normalizedQuery = deburr(query.toLowerCase());

    const filtered = query
      ? options.filter((option) =>

        )
      : options;

    return filtered.sort((a, b) => {
      const aSelected = selectedKeys.includes(a.key);
      const bSelected = selectedKeys.includes(b.key);

      // Selected items come first
      if (aSelected && !bSelected) {
        return -1;
      }
      if (!aSelected && bSelected) {
        return 1;
      }

      // If both have the same selection state and there's a query,
      // sort options starting with query first
      if (query) {
        const aStartsWith = deburr(a.label)
          .toLowerCase()
          .startsWith(normalizedQuery);
        const bStartsWith = deburr(b.label)
          .toLowerCase()
          .startsWith(normalizedQuery);

        if (aStartsWith && !bStartsWith) {
          return -1;
        }
        if (!aStartsWith && bStartsWith) {
          return 1;
        }
      }

      return 0;
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-07 01:04:24Z)**_

I read the relevant code to see what each option needs in practice. Both are workable, but each needs more than "drop in the component."

## Shared problem: `FilterOptions` wasn't built for this

[FilterOptions.tsx](app/components/FilterOptions.tsx) affects both options in the same ways:

- **The menu closes on every click.** Each item calls `onSelect(option.key)` and then `setOpen(false)` (lines 74–77). You can't put inputs or a calendar inside the menu.
- **The label comes from the option list.** The trigger finds `selectedKeys` in `options` and shows that option's `label`. To show "Mar 1 – May 31, 2025," `DateFilter` has to add a `custom` option whose label is computed from the dates.
- **"Custom range" chosen but no dates yet.** If you store `dateFilter=custom` in the URL to remember the user's choice, the API rejects it, because [schema.ts:42-47](server/routes/api/documents/schema.ts#L42-L47) only allows `day|week|month|year`. Either keep "picking" as local state in `DateFilter`, or remove `custom` before sending the request.
- **Mobile uses a different container.** Phones get a bottom-sheet Drawer instead of a dropdown (lines 263–282), so whatever opens next has to work after a drawer closes as well as after a menu closes.

So in both options, `DateFilter.tsx` handles `onSelect("custom")` itself instead of [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]ing it up, and then shows the date inputs.

---

## Option 1: Built-in date inputs

### How it would look
Choosing "Custom range" shows two `<input type="date">` fields **directly in the filter bar**, next to the dropdown. They're added to the existing `<Flex>` in [Search.tsx:302-307](app/scenes/Search/Search.tsx#L302-L307). Because nothing has to open after the menu closes, you avoid the popover timing problem entirely.

```tsx
{showCustom && (
  <>
    <DateInput type="date" value={dateFrom} max={dateTo || today}
      onChange={(e) => onRangeChange({ dateFrom: e.target.value })} />
    <span>–</span>
    <DateInput type="date" value={dateTo} min={dateFrom} max={today}
      onChange={(e) => onRangeChange({ dateTo: e.target.value })} />
  </>
)}
```

### What I found
- **Outline's `Input` component doesn't support `type="date"` yet.** Its allowed types are `"text" | "email" | "checkbox" | "search" | "textarea" | "[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]word"` ([Input.tsx:160](app/components/Input.tsx#L160)). Either add `"date"` there (one line, but it changes a shared component), or use a styled plain `<input>`.
- **The app doesn't use built-in date inputs anywhere yet,** so there's no existing styling to copy. Dark mode needs `color-scheme: dark` so the calendar icon and popup don't render as light-on-light.

### Advantages
- **Simple value format.** The value is always `"YYYY-MM-DD"` whatever the user's language, which matches the URL format (`?dateFrom=2025-03-01`).
- **Validation comes for free.** `min`/`max` stop the browser from offering invalid days, and `onChange` only fires for a complete, valid date or `""` (cleared). Half-typed dates never reach your code.
- **Open ends are natural:** just leave one field empty.
- **Mobile works well:** iOS and Android show their own wheel or calendar pickers. You'd use the same component on every screen size.
- **Typing old dates is fast,** with no clicking through years.

### Gotchas
- ⚠️ **Time zone trap:** `new Date("2025-03-01")` is read as **UTC midnight**, not local midnight. For a user in New York that's 7 pm on Feb 28. Use `parseISO` from date-fns (already a dependency), which reads it as local time, then `startOfDay` / `endOfDay`.
- **Searches fire on every change.** Each change rewrites the URL and runs a new search, so typing one date can trigger several searches. You may want to debounce, or only update the URL when the input loses focus.
- **Inconsistent display:** the date format follows the browser's language (e.g. `03/01/2025` vs `01/03/2025`), not the user's Outline language setting. The calendar popup also looks different in Chrome, Safari and Firefox.
- **Crowded filter bar:** two inputs add about 280px. On mobile the filters wrap, so check the layout.

### Effort
About **30–50 lines** in `DateFilter.tsx` and `Search.tsx`, plus a small styled component. Low risk.

---

## Option 2: Calendar in range mode, in a popover

### How it would look
Choosing "Custom range" closes the menu and opens a popover attached to the dropdown button. The popover contains `<Calendar mode="range" />` with Clear and Apply buttons at the bottom.

```tsx
<Popover open={pickerOpen} onOpenChange={setPickerOpen}>
  <PopoverAnchor asChild>
    <span><FilterOptions options={options} onSelect={handleSelect} ... /></span>
  </PopoverAnchor>
  <PopoverContent width={300} shrink aria-label={t("Choose a date range")}>
    <Calendar
      mode="range"
      selected={draft}            // { from?: Date; to?: Date }
      onSelect={setDraft}
      locale={locale}
      disabled={{ after: new Date() }}
      captionLayout="dropdown"
      fromYear={2016} toYear={new Date().getFullYear()}
    />
    <Footer>
      <Button neutral onClick={clear}>{t("Clear")}</Button>
      <Button onClick={apply} disabled={!draft?.from}>{t("Apply")}</Button>
    </Footer>
  </PopoverContent>
</Popover>
```

### What I found
- **The building blocks exist.** The [Popover](app/components/primitives/Popover.tsx) wraps Radix and exports `PopoverAnchor`, so you can attach a popover to an existing button without making it the trigger. [ExpiryDatePicker.tsx](app/scenes/ApiKeyNew/components/ExpiryDatePicker.tsx) shows how to set up the user's language (`useUserLocale` + `dateLocale`).
- **The installed library is react-day-picker 8.10.2.** In v8, range mode gives you `{ from, to }`, and month/year dropdowns need `captionLayout="dropdown"` **plus** `fromYear`/`toYear` (or `fromDate`/`toDate`). Without those, the dropdowns don't appear.
- ⚠️ **[Calendar.tsx](shared/components/Calendar.tsx) has no range styling.** It only styles `.rdp-day_selected` as a solid filled circle. In range mode, v8 gives *every* day in the range the `selected` class, so a range would look like a row of separate filled circles, not a band. You'd need about 15–25 lines of CSS for `.rdp-day_range_start`, `.rdp-day_range_middle` and `.rdp-day_range_end`, e.g. square middle days with a lighter accent background.
- ⚠️ **Calendar.tsx also has no styles for the month/year dropdowns** (`.rdp-caption_dropdowns`, `.rdp-dropdown`). They'd show up as unstyled `<select>`s, and the hidden-label class is the only part of the library's stylesheet that has been recreated. That's another 15–20 lines of CSS. These changes are in a **shared** component used by `ExpiryDatePicker` and the editor's date mentions, so check that those still look right.
- ⚠️ **Focus conflict:** when a Radix menu closes, it moves focus back to its trigger button. If your popover opens at the same moment, the two can fight: the popover may close immediately or lose focus. `FilterOptions` doesn't expose `onCloseAutoFocus` to prevent this, so you'd either add a prop to it or delay opening the popover by one tick (`requestAnimationFrame` / `setTimeout(0)`). It's a small fix, but it needs testing on desktop and on the mobile drawer.

### Advantages
- **Looks native to Outline:** the same calendar as API key expiry and date mentions, in the user's own language.
- **Clear selection:** the user sees the whole range, and the Apply button means only one search runs.
- **Built-in keyboard support:** `react-day-picker` handles arrow keys, Page Up/Down for months, and screen-reader labels.
- **Works with dates directly:** the selection is already `Date` objects in local time, so there's no UTC parsing trap. You still format them as `YYYY-MM-DD` for the URL.

### Gotchas
- **Open ends need a rule.** With only a start date chosen, you could apply it as "from this date to now." Leaving the start open ("everything before X") has no natural gesture.
- **Selecting one day:** confirm how v8 handles clicking the same day twice (it should give `from === to`). Also check what happens when the user clicks a date before the current start.
- **Keeping the draft in sync:** keep a separate draft range while the popover is open, and fill it from the URL each time the popover opens, so cancelling doesn't leave stale dates.
- **Mobile:** a 300px popover fits on a phone, but test it after the drawer closes, not just after the menu closes.

### Effort
About **80–120 lines**: `DateFilter.tsx` (~50–70), Calendar CSS (~30–45), and `Search.tsx` (~15). Medium risk, mainly from the focus conflict and the shared CSS.

---

## Side by side

| | Option 1: built-in inputs | Option 2: range calendar |
|---|---|---|
| Lines (frontend) | ~30–50 | ~80–120 |
| Touches shared components | `Input` type list (optional) | `Calendar` CSS (required) |
| Popover / focus handling | None (inputs are inline) | Yes (menu → popover hand-off) |
| Looks like Outline | ❌ Varies by browser | ✅ |
| Matches user's language | Browser language | ✅ Outline language |
| Open-ended ranges | ✅ Leave a field empty | Start-only workable, end-only awkward |
| Picking old dates | ✅ Type it | OK with month/year dropdowns |
| Mobile | ✅ Phone's own picker | Popover after drawer, needs testing |
| Searches per change | Every edit (debounce) | One, on Apply |
| Main pitfall | UTC parsing of `"YYYY-MM-DD"` | Shared CSS + focus conflict |

## Recommendation
- **For a "Small" issue in a class project,** Option 1 is the safer first version. It's less code, nothing has to open after the menu closes, open ends are easy, and the only real trap is a one-line `parseISO` fix.
- **Option 2 is the nicer result.** It's worth doing if you have time to style the range band and test the focus hand-off on desktop and mobile. The backend is identical for both, so you can ship Option 1 and switch later without touching the API.

Whichever you pick, add two acceptance criteria to the spec: "Dates are interpreted in the user's local time zone," and "A custom range that has been chosen survives a page refresh."

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-07 01:09:37Z)**_

There are four main ways to do it. All of them keep plain dates in the URL (`?dateFrom=2025-03-01&dateTo=2025-05-31`), which satisfies the spec's URL criterion. They differ in **where** "March 1" gets turned into an exact moment in time.

While checking, I found that Outline already stores each user's time zone. [AuthStore.ts:250-254](app/stores/AuthStore.ts#L250-L254) reads it from the browser and saves it to `user.timezone` ([server/models/User.ts:225](server/models/User.ts#L225)) whenever it changes. There's also a `zodTimezone()` validator in [users/schema.ts:99](server/routes/api/users/schema.ts#L99). That makes Options C and D more practical than they'd usually be.

## A. The browser converts dates to exact timestamps
The browser turns each date into the start (or end) of that day in the user's local time and sends ISO timestamps:
```ts
dateFrom: startOfDay(parseISO("2025-03-01")).toISOString() // "2025-03-01T05:00:00.000Z" in New York
dateTo:   endOfDay(parseISO("2025-05-31")).toISOString()
```
- ✅ The server does no time zone logic. It just compares `updatedAt` with two timestamps.
- ✅ Uses date-fns, which is already installed, and needs no new libraries.
- ✅ Precise and easy to test on the server.
- ❌ API users have to work out the timestamps themselves. Validate them with `z.iso.datetime()`.
- ❌ A shared link is interpreted in each viewer's time zone, so results can differ slightly across time zones. Arguably that's correct.

## B. The server treats plain dates as UTC
The API accepts `"2025-03-01"`, and the server uses UTC midnight.
- ✅ Simplest code, and the API is easy to read.
- ✅ A shared link gives identical results for everyone.
- ❌ Results are off by hours for most users. Someone in California who edits a document at 6 pm on May 31 would find it missing from a range ending May 31, because it's already June 1 in UTC. Plenty of students test in the evening, so this kind of bug would actually get noticed.

## C. The server uses the user's stored time zone
The API accepts plain dates, and the server reads them in `user.timezone`.
- ✅ Clean API with correct local-time results.
- ✅ Reuses data Outline already keeps up to date.
- ❌ More server work. No time zone library like `date-fns-tz` is installed, so you'd either add one or convert in Postgres (`AT TIME ZONE`).
- ❌ `timezone` can be null for new users or API keys, so you need a fallback, probably UTC.
- ❌ Daylight saving time makes tests harder to write.
- ❌ Results depend on hidden user data, which makes bugs harder to trace.

## D. The browser sends plain dates plus a `timeZone` parameter
For example: `{ dateFrom: "2025-03-01", dateTo: "2025-05-31", timeZone: "America/New_York" }`.
- ✅ Explicit and doesn't depend on stored data. You can reuse `zodTimezone()`.
- ✅ The API is readable, and callers can choose a time zone.
- ❌ Same server-side conversion work as Option C.
- ❌ One more parameter to validate, test and document.

## Comparison

| | Where conversion happens | Server complexity | Correct for user | API readability |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | Browser | Low | ✅ | Timestamps |
| B | Server (UTC) | Lowest | ❌ Off by hours | Plain dates |
| C | Server (`user.timezone`) | High | ✅ (if set) | Plain dates |
| D | Server ([REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]ed in) | High | ✅ | Plain dates + zone |

## Recommendation
Go with **Option A**. It's correct, needs no new dependencies, and keeps all the time zone handling in about 4 lines on the frontend. That fits the "Small" scope.

Two details for whichever option you choose:
- **End date:** compare with `updatedAt < start of the next day` instead of `<= 23:59:59.999`, which avoids millisecond edge cases. With Option A, send `addDays(startOfDay(to), 1)` and use `Op.lt` on the server.
- **Parsing:** never use `new Date("2025-03-01")`, because it reads the date as UTC. Use `parseISO`.

```text
  searchTitles = async (options?: SearchParams): Promise<SearchResult[]> => {
    const compactedOptions = omitBy(options, (o) => !o);
    const res = await client.post("/documents.search_titles", {
      ...compactedOptions,
    });
    invariant(res?.data, "Search response should be available");

    // add the documents and associated policies to the store
    runInAction("DocumentsStore#searchTitles", () => {
      res.data.forEach(this.add);
      this.addPolicies(res.policies);
    });

    // store a reference to the document model in the search cache instead
    // of the original result from the API.
    const results: SearchResult[] = compact(
      res.data.map((result: SearchResult) => {
        const document = this.data.get(result.id);
        if (!document) {
          return null;
        }
        return {
          id: document.id,
          document,
        };
      })
    );
    return results;
  };

  @action
  search = async (options: SearchParams): Promise<SearchResult[]> => {
    const compactedOptions = omitBy(options, (o) => !o);
    const res = await client.post("/documents.search", {
      ...compactedOptions,
    });
    invariant(res?.data, "Search response should be available");

    // add the documents and associated policies to the store
    runInAction("DocumentsStore#search", () => {
      res.data.forEach((result: SearchResult) => this.add(result.document));
      this.addPolicies(res.policies);
    });
```

I traced every place the current `dateFilter` touches. With Option A, **9 files change and none are new**: 4 server files, 3 frontend files, the translation file, and 2 test files.

## Server

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| [server/routes/api/documents/schema.ts](server/routes/api/documents/schema.ts#L51) | Add `dateFrom` / `dateTo` (`z.iso.datetime().optional()`) to **`BaseSearchSchema`** (line 51), not `DateFilterSchema`. `DateFilterSchema` is also used by the Drafts endpoint (line 136), so adding them there would bring Drafts into scope. Add a `.refine()` that rejects from > to, and one that rejects a preset combined with a range. |
| [server/utils/BaseSearchProvider.ts](server/utils/BaseSearchProvider.ts#L36) | Add `dateFrom?: Date` and `dateTo?: Date` to `SearchOptions`. |
| [plugins/search-postgres/server/PostgresSearchProvider.ts](plugins/search-postgres/server/PostgresSearchProvider.ts#L669) | In `buildWhere()`, next to the existing `dateFilter` block, add `updatedAt: { [Op.gte]: dateFrom }` / `{ [Op.lt]: dateTo }`. **One change covers everything:** `buildWhere` is shared by all three search methods (lines 189, 282, 385). |
| [server/routes/api/documents/documents.ts](server/routes/api/documents/documents.ts#L988) | Read `dateFrom`/`dateTo` from `ctx.input.body` and [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] them to the provider in `documents.search_titles` (~line 988) and in both branches of `documents.search`, the shared-link and normal paths (~lines 1102 and 1149). |

## Frontend

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| [app/scenes/Search/components/DateFilter.tsx](app/scenes/Search/components/DateFilter.tsx) | Add the "Custom range" option, with a label computed from the dates when active. Show the two `<input type="date">` fields with `min`/`max` and a validation message when From > To. |
| [app/scenes/Search/Search.tsx](app/scenes/Search/Search.tsx#L70) | Read `dateFrom`/`dateTo` from the URL (line 70), add them to the `filters` memo (lines 93–116) and to `handleFilterChange`'s type (line 168), and [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] them to `<DateFilter>` (line 305). **This is where Option A's conversion happens:** turn `"2025-03-01"` into `startOfDay(parseISO(...)).toISOString()` and the end date into `addDays(startOfDay(parseISO(...)), 1).toISOString()` before the request. Choosing a preset should also clear the range. |
| [app/stores/DocumentsStore.ts](app/stores/DocumentsStore.ts#L36) | Add `dateFrom?: string` and `dateTo?: string` to the `SearchParams` type. That's all: `search()` and `searchTitles()` already [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] every option straight to the API (lines 400–435). |
| [shared/i18n/locales/en_US/translation.json](shared/i18n/locales/en_US/translation.json#L1109) | Add strings: "Custom range", "From", "To", and the validation message. Outline may generate this file with a script, so check `package.json` for an i18n extract command rather than editing by hand. |

## Tests

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| [server/routes/api/documents/documents.test.ts](server/routes/api/documents/documents.test.ts#L1199) | API tests next to the existing `dateFilter` tests (lines 1199, 1384, 1915): a valid range, only From, only To, both end dates included, from > to returns 400, an invalid date returns 400, and preset + range returns 400. |
| [plugins/search-postgres/server/PostgresSearchProvider.test.ts](plugins/search-postgres/server/PostgresSearchProvider.test.ts) | Optional but recommended: unit-test that `buildWhere` filters correctly at the boundaries, e.g. a document updated exactly at `dateTo` is excluded. |

## Files that don't change
- **[shared/types.ts](shared/types.ts#L16):** `DateFilter` stays as `"day" | "week" | "month" | "year"`. The range uses separate fields and doesn't extend this type.
- **[FilterOptions.tsx](app/components/FilterOptions.tsx):** with Option A, the inputs sit next to the dropdown, so the shared component doesn't need changes.
- **[Drafts.tsx](app/scenes/Drafts.tsx), the `documents.drafts` handler, and the browser-side drafts filter in `DocumentsStore`:** Drafts is out of scope. Putting the schema change in `BaseSearchSchema` keeps it that way.

```text
/**
 * Formats a Date into a date-only ISO string (yyyy-MM-dd) in the local
 * timezone. Used as the stored value for date mentions.
 *
 * @param date The date to format.
 * @returns the date-only ISO string.
 */
export function toISODate(date: Date): string {
  return format(date, "yyyy-MM-dd");
}

/**
 * Parses a date-only ISO string (yyyy-MM-dd) into a Date at local midnight.
 * Strings carrying a time component are rejected so the date-only contract
 * (and the day-granular comparisons that depend on it) cannot be violated.
 *
 * @param iso The date-only ISO string.
 * @returns the parsed Date at local midnight, or null when the string is not a
 * valid date-only value.
 */
export function parseISODate(iso: string): Date | null {
  if (!/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(iso)) {
    return null;
  }
  const date = parseISO(iso);
  return isValid(date) ? date : null;
}

/**
 * Formats a date mention's stored ISO value into an absolute, localized,
 * human-readable label. The year is omitted within the current year (e.g.
 * "January 2nd") and included otherwise (e.g. "February 3rd, 2024"). Suitable
 * for plaintext and markdown serialization.
 *
 * @param iso The date-only ISO string.
 * @param language The user's language preference.
 * @returns the absolute human-readable date, or the original string when invalid.
 */
export function dateToReadable(
  flex: 1;
  padding: 8px 12px 8px
    ${(props) => (props.hasPrefix ? 0 : props.hasIcon ? "8px" : "12px")};

  ${(props) => props.$maxHeight && `max-height: ${props.$maxHeight};`}

  &:disabled,
  &::placeholder {
    color: ${s("placeholder")};
    opacity: 1;
  }
`;
```

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="Write"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Write**</summary>

```typescript
import { format as formatDate } from "date-fns";
import { useMemo, useState } from "react";
import { useTranslation } from "react-i18next";
import styled from "styled-components";
import { s } from "@shared/styles";
import type { DateFilter as TDateFilter } from "@shared/types";
import { dateLocale, parseISODate, toISODate } from "@shared/utils/date";
import FilterOptions from "~/components/FilterOptions";
import Text from "~/components/Text";
import useUserLocale from "~/hooks/useUserLocale";

/** Option key used for the custom date range, never sent to the API. */
const CustomRangeKey = "custom";

type DateRange = {
  dateFrom?: string;
  dateTo?: string;
};

type Props = {
  /** The selected date filter */
  dateFilter?: string | null;
  /** The start of the custom range (yyyy-MM-dd), inclusive */
  dateFrom?: string;
  /** The end of the custom range (yyyy-MM-dd), inclusive */
  dateTo?: string;
  /** Callback when a date filter is selected */
  onSelect: (key: TDateFilter) => void;
  /** Callback when the custom range changes */
  onRangeChange: (range: DateRange) => void;
};

const DateFilter = ({
  dateFilter,
  dateFrom = "",
  dateTo = "",
  onSelect,
  onRangeChange,
}: Props) => {
  const { t } = useTranslation();
  const userLocale = useUserLocale();
  const locale = dateLocale(userLocale);
  const hasRange = !!(dateFrom || dateTo);
  const [showRange, setShowRange] = useState(hasRange);
  const isCustom = showRange || hasRange;

  const from = parseISODate(dateFrom);
  const to = parseISODate(dateTo);
  const isInvalid = !!(from && to && from > to);
  const today = toISODate(new Date());

  const customLabel = useMemo(() => {
    const fromLabel = from && formatDate(from, "MMM d, yyyy", { locale });
    const toLabel = to && formatDate(to, "MMM d, yyyy", { locale });

    if (fromLabel && toLabel) {
      return `${fromLabel} – ${toLabel}`;
    }
    if (fromLabel) {
      return t("Since {{ date }}", { date: fromLabel });
    }
    if (toLabel) {
      return t("Until {{ date }}", { date: toLabel });
    }
    return t("Custom range");
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [dateFrom, dateTo, locale, t]);

  const options = useMemo(
    () => [
      {
        key: "",
        label: t("All time"),
      },
      {
        key: "day",
        label: t("Past day"),
      },
      {
        key: "week",
        label: t("Past week"),
      },
      {
        key: "month",
        label: t("Past month"),
      },
      {
        key: "year",
        label: t("Past year"),
      },
      {
        key: CustomRangeKey,
        label: customLabel,
      },
    ],
    [t, customLabel]
  );

  const handleSelect = (key: string | null | undefined) => {
    if (key === CustomRangeKey) {
      setShowRange(true);
      if (!hasRange) {
        // Clear any preset so it does not keep filtering the results.
        onRangeChange({});
      }
      return;
    }

    setShowRange(false);
    onSelect(key as TDateFilter);
  };

  return (
    <>
      <FilterOptions
        options={options}
        selectedKeys={[isCustom ? CustomRangeKey : dateFilter]}
        onSelect={handleSelect}
        defaultLabel={t("Any time")}
      />
      {isCustom && (
        <Range>
          <Label>
            {t("From")}
            <DateInput
              type="date"
              value={dateFrom}
              max={dateTo || today}
              onChange={(ev) =>
                onRangeChange({ dateFrom: ev.target.value || undefined })
              }
            />
          </Label>
          <Label>
            {t("To")}
            <DateInput
              type="date"
              value={dateTo}
              min={dateFrom || undefined}
              max={today}
              onChange={(ev) =>
                onRangeChange({ dateTo: ev.target.value || undefined })
              }
            />
          </Label>
          {isInvalid && (
            <Text type="danger" size="small" role="alert">
              {t("The start date must be on or before the end date")}
            </Text>
          )}
        </Range>
      )}
    </>
  );
};

const Range = styled.div`
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 8px;
  margin: 0 8px;
`;

const Label = styled.label`
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 6px;
  font-size: 14px;
  color: ${s("textSecondary")};
`;

const DateInput = styled.input`
  height: 28px;
  padding: 0 6px;
  border: 1px solid ${s("inputBorder")};
  border-radius: 4px;
  background: none;
  color: ${s("text")};
  font-family: inherit;
  font-size: 14px;
  color-scheme: ${(props) => (props.theme.isDark ? "dark" : "light")};

  &:focus {
    outline: none;
    border-color: ${s("inputBorderFocused")};
  }
`;

export default DateFilter;

```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-07 16:02:10Z)**_

The custom date range is built, but I haven't run the API tests or tried it in the browser. The tests need Postgres and Redis, and neither is running because Docker isn't running.

**What's checked:**
- The project type check now [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]es. The first run caught that the Drafts page also uses `DateFilter`, so "Custom range" now only appears where the page supports it. Drafts looks and behaves the same as before, which keeps it out of scope as the spec says.
- A temporary test of the request validation [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]ed: a valid range and a start-only or end-only range are accepted. The API rejects a start date after the end date, an invalid date, and a preset combined with a range.
- The date conversion is correct in New York time, including the daylight-saving change.
- Lint is clean apart from two warnings in `Search.tsx` that were already there.

**How it works:**
- **API:** new `dateFrom`/`dateTo` parameters for search and title search. The end is exclusive: the page sends the start of the day after the chosen end date.
- **Search page:** the URL holds plain dates (`?dateFrom=2025-03-01&dateTo=2025-05-31`). The page turns them into the start of each local day using Outline's existing `parseISODate` helper. If the start date is after the end date, the range isn't sent and a warning shows under the inputs.
- **Dropdown:** a new "Custom range" option shows labeled From and To date inputs. The dropdown label becomes "Mar 1, 2025 – May 31, 2025", "Since …" or "Until …". Choosing a preset clears the range, and choosing "Custom range" clears any preset.

**Changes from what I described earlier:**
- I didn't add the optional search-provider unit test. The API tests check the boundaries: a document updated at exactly the start time is included, and one at exactly the end time is excluded.
- I added the English strings to the translation file by hand, because Outline's string-extraction script fails on Windows.

To test it yourself, start Docker Desktop and the test database, then run `yarn test:server server/routes/api/documents/documents.test.ts`. After that, open search in the app and try a few ranges.

Nothing is committed yet. `.vscode/settings.json` was already modified when I started, and I left it alone.

A search for "onboarding" on **Sep 9** returns nothing, because it was last edited on Sep 11. That's correct behavior under the approved spec, which lists "Filtering by created date instead of last-updated date" as **out of scope**.

To check that same-day ranges work:

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-07 16:25:02Z)**_

Good, that explains it. One thing to know so it doesn't look like a bug later: drafts aren't excluded from date-range searches. Search includes drafts by default, because the document type filter starts with both Published and Draft selected. A draft can still disappear for one of these reasons:

- **Its last-updated date is outside the range.** For example, `sssss` was last updated Sep 15 at 8:01 pm EDT, so it shows for Sep 15 but not Sep 16. That's because the page uses your local time zone, while the database stores times in UTC (`00:01` on Sep 16).
- **The document type filter has Draft unchecked.**
- **Someone else wrote it.** Drafts are only visible to their author, so another user's draft never appears in your search results.

If a draft that's yours and in range appears without the date filter but disappears with it, that would be a real bug, so tell me if you see that.

I'm leaving the single-day test in `documents.test.ts` (in both copies) as extra coverage. Nothing is committed yet. I can commit it on `feat-filter_by_date_range` if you want.

```text
    if (collectionIds.length) {
      where[Op.or].push({ collectionId: collectionIds });
    }

    if (options.dateFilter) {
      where[Op.and].push({
        updatedAt: {
          [Op.gt]: sequelize.literal(
            `now() - interval '1 ${options.dateFilter}'`
          ),
        },
      });
    }

    if (options.dateFrom) {
      where[Op.and].push({
        updatedAt: {
          [Op.gte]: options.dateFrom,
        },
      });
    }

    if (options.dateTo) {
      where[Op.and].push({
        updatedAt: {
          [Op.lt]: options.dateTo,
        },
      });
    }

    if (options.collaboratorIds) {
      where[Op.and].push({
        collaboratorIds: {
          [Op.contains]: options.collaboratorIds,
        },
      });
    }

    if (options.documentIds) {
      where[Op.and].push({
        id: options.documentIds,
      });
    }

    const statusQuery = [];
    if (options.statusFilter?.includes(StatusFilter.Published)) {
      statusQuery.push({
        [Op.and]: [
          {
            publishedAt: {
              [Op.ne]: null,
            },
            archivedAt: {
              [Op.eq]: null,
            },
          },
        ],
      });
    }

    if (
      options.statusFilter?.includes(StatusFilter.Draft) &&
      // Only ever include draft results for the user's own documents
      model instanceof User
    ) {
      statusQuery.push({
        [Op.and]: [
          {
            publishedAt: {
              [Op.eq]: null,
            },
            archivedAt: {
              [Op.eq]: null,
            },
            [Op.or]: [
              { createdById: model.id },
              { "$memberships.id$": { [Op.ne]: null } },
            ],
          },
        ],
      });
    }

    if (options.statusFilter?.includes(StatusFilter.Archived)) {
      statusQuery.push({
        archivedAt: {
          [Op.ne]: null,
        },
      });
    }

    if (statusQuery.length) {
      where[Op.and].push({
        [Op.or]: statusQuery,
      });
    }
```
</details></tool-use>

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-07 16:28:03Z)**_

Yes, the date range only looks at the **last-updated** date. That explains what you're seeing.

`Notion but live` was **created on Sep 9** but **last updated on Sep 11** (3:26 pm your time). I think you mean September, since the database shows Sep 9 and there's no November date. So:

| Range | Shows the draft? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Sep 9 – Sep 9 | ❌ | Last updated Sep 11, outside the range |
| Sep 9 – Sep 11 (or later) | ✅ | Sep 11 is inside the range |
| Sep 11 – Sep 11 | ✅ | Same day as the last update |
| Sep 12 – anything | ❌ | Starts after the last update |

So "ranges beginning on Sep 9" only work if they extend to Sep 11.

That's what the approved spec asks for:
- Acceptance criterion 3: *"…only documents whose **last-updated** date falls within it"*
- Out of Scope: *"Filtering by **created date** instead of last-updated date"*

It also matches the existing presets: "Past week" means "edited in the past week."

If you think users will expect created dates, it's worth raising with whoever owns the spec. Supporting both would be a product decision, e.g. a "Created / Updated" toggle next to the range. Technically it's a small change (filter on `createdAt` instead of, or as well as, `updatedAt`), but it's outside the current scope, so I wouldn't add it without their approval.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-07 17:33:38Z)**_

The commit changes 9 files. Here's what changed in each one and why, server first, then frontend, then translations and tests.

## Server

### [server/routes/api/documents/schema.ts](server/routes/api/documents/schema.ts)
**What changed:**
- Added two optional fields, `dateFrom` and `dateTo`, to `BaseSearchSchema`. Both use `z.coerce.date()`, so the API accepts timestamp strings and turns them into `Date` objects. An invalid date like `"not a date"` fails validation.
- Added a helper, `withDateRangeValidation`, with two rules:
  - `dateFrom` must be earlier than `dateTo`.
  - `dateFilter` can't be combined with `dateFrom` or `dateTo`.
- Wrapped `DocumentsSearchSchema` and `DocumentsSearchTitlesSchema` in that helper.

**Why:**
- Criterion 9 says the API must accept the new parameters and reject invalid dates with a 400 error.
- **Why `BaseSearchSchema`:** the fields went there instead of the existing `DateFilterSchema`, because the Drafts endpoint also uses `DateFilterSchema`. Adding them there would have brought Drafts into scope, which the spec excludes.
- **Why a wrapper:** the rules live in a wrapper instead of on `BaseSearchSchema` itself, because Zod 4 won't let you `.extend()` a schema that has refinements, and both search schemas extend `BaseSearchSchema`.
- **Why the second rule:** rejecting a preset combined with a range keeps the API's behavior clear instead of quietly picking one.
- `z.coerce.date()` matches how other date fields in this codebase are validated, e.g. `startDate` and `endDate` on the insights endpoint.

### [server/utils/BaseSearchProvider.ts](server/utils/BaseSearchProvider.ts)
**What changed:** added optional `dateFrom?: Date` and `dateTo?: Date` to the `SearchOptions` type, with doc comments saying that `dateFrom` is inclusive and `dateTo` is exclusive.

**Why:** `SearchOptions` is the contract between the API handlers and the search engine. Without these fields, TypeScript wouldn't allow [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]ing the range to the provider.

### [plugins/search-postgres/server/PostgresSearchProvider.ts](plugins/search-postgres/server/PostgresSearchProvider.ts)
**What changed:** in `buildWhere()`, right after the existing `dateFilter` block, added two conditions:
- `updatedAt >= dateFrom` (`Op.gte`)
- `updatedAt < dateTo` (`Op.lt`)

Each is added only if its value is present.

**Why:**
- This is where the database query is built.
- **One change covers everything:** `buildWhere()` is shared by all three search methods (search for a user, search for a team through a shared link, and title-only search), so this one change covers every search path.
- **Last-updated date:** filtering on `updatedAt` matches the spec's "last-updated date" requirement and how the existing presets already work.
- **Exclusive end:** the browser sends the start of the day after the chosen end date, which includes the whole end date without millisecond edge cases.
- **Optional conditions:** each condition is only added when its value is present, which is what makes open-ended ranges ("since X" or "until Y") work.
- **Bound values:** the dates are [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]ed as values, not pasted into SQL with `sequelize.literal` the way the preset does it. Range dates come from the user, so they should never become SQL text.

### [server/routes/api/documents/documents.ts](server/routes/api/documents/documents.ts)
**What changed:** in the `documents.search_titles` handler and in both branches of the `documents.search` handler (shared link and logged-in user), the handlers now read `dateFrom` and `dateTo` from the validated request and [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] them to the search provider next to `dateFilter`.

**Why:** the handlers sit between the validated request and the search provider. Without [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]ing the values through, the schema would accept them but they'd never reach the query. The shared-link branch was included so filtering works the same whether you're logged in or searching a publicly shared collection.

## Frontend

### [app/stores/DocumentsStore.ts](app/stores/DocumentsStore.ts)
**What changed:** added optional `dateFrom?: string` and `dateTo?: string` to the `SearchParams` type, with comments noting they're ISO timestamps.

**Why:** `Search.tsx` [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]es its filters through this type to `documents.search()` and `documents.searchTitles()`. Those methods already forward every option to the API, so no logic changes were needed, only the type.

### [app/scenes/Search/Search.tsx](app/scenes/Search/Search.tsx)
**What changed:**
- Added a helper, `toDateRangeParams()`, that turns the plain dates from the URL (e.g. `2025-03-01`) into timestamps for the API. It uses Outline's existing `parseISODate` to get **local** midnight for the start date, and adds one day to the end date to get the exclusive end. It returns nothing if the start date is after the end date, so an invalid range isn't applied.
- Reads `dateFrom` and `dateTo` from the URL next to the other filters.
- In the `filters` object sent with each search, includes the converted range only when no preset is selected.
- Adds `dateFrom` and `dateTo` to `handleFilterChange`'s type.
- Passes the dates to `<DateFilter>` with two callbacks:
  - **Choosing a preset** clears the range.
  - **Changing the range** clears the preset.

**Why:**
- **Time zone:** this is where the local time zone choice (Option A) is implemented. Using `parseISODate` instead of `new Date("2025-03-01")` avoids the bug where JavaScript reads a bare date as UTC midnight, which for Eastern time is the evening of the day before.
- **Shareable links:** keeping plain dates in the URL makes links readable and satisfies criterion 7 (refresh or share the link and keep the filter). The page already treats the URL as the source of truth for all filters.
- **Preset vs. range:** criterion 8 says choosing a preset clears the custom range. Choosing a custom range clears the preset so the two never conflict, and preferring the preset when both are in the URL avoids a 400 error from a hand-edited link.
- **Invalid ranges:** returning nothing for a reversed range satisfies criterion 5 ("the filter is not applied").

### [app/scenes/Search/components/DateFilter.tsx](app/scenes/Search/components/DateFilter.tsx)
**What changed:**
- **New option:** added "Custom range" to the dropdown, along with new props for the range values and a range-change callback.
- **Label:** when a range is active, the dropdown label shows:
  - "Mar 1, 2025 – May 31, 2025" for a full range
  - "Since Mar 1, 2025" for a start date only
  - "Until May 31, 2025" for an end date only

  Dates are formatted in the user's language through `useUserLocale` and `dateLocale`.
- **Inputs:** choosing Custom range shows two labeled `<input type="date">` fields, From and To, next to the dropdown.
  - **Limits:** `max` stops future dates, and `min`/`max` stop To from being earlier than From in the picker.
  - **Error message:** if a typed From date is later than To, a red message appears.
  - **Styling:** the inputs use Outline's theme colors and switch `color-scheme` in dark mode so the calendar icon stays visible.
- **Drafts page:** the range-change callback is optional, and "Custom range" only appears when it's provided.

**Why:**
- This is the visible part of the feature, covering criteria 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6.
- **Built-in inputs:** chose browser date inputs (Option 1) placed inline instead of a calendar popover, because the shared dropdown closes on every click and couldn't host inputs. Inline inputs avoid timing problems between the menu and a popover, leaving one end empty is natural, and phones use their own date pickers.
- **Optional callback:** the type check found that the Drafts page uses the same component. Making the callback optional keeps Drafts exactly as before, as the spec requires.
- **Remembering the choice:** a small piece of local state remembers that "Custom range" was chosen before any dates are entered. Otherwise the inputs would disappear immediately, since the URL has no dates yet.

## Translations

### [shared/i18n/locales/en_US/translation.json](shared/i18n/locales/en_US/translation.json)
**What changed:** added six English strings: "Since {{ date }}", "Until {{ date }}", "Custom range", "From", "To", and "The start date must be on or before the end date". They sit next to the existing date filter strings.

**Why:** Outline [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]es all visible text through its translation system (`t()`), and new strings need entries in the English file. They were added by hand because Outline's string-extraction script fails on Windows.

## Tests

### [server/routes/api/documents/documents.test.ts](server/routes/api/documents/documents.test.ts)
**What changed:**
- In the `documents.search` tests, added a "custom date range" group with two helpers: one creates documents with set update times, and one sorts result titles for comparison. It has seven tests:
  - **Range with boundaries:** a range includes a document updated exactly at the start time and excludes one updated exactly at the end time or just before the start.
  - **Single day:** a one-day range includes that day's document and excludes its neighbors.
  - **Start only:** works on its own.
  - **End only:** works on its own.
  - **Start after end:** returns 400 with the matching message.
  - **Invalid date:** returns 400.
  - **Preset plus range:** returns 400 with the matching message.
- In the `documents.search_titles` tests, added one test that title-only search also respects the range.

**Why:**
- Criterion 11 requires tests for valid ranges, open-ended ranges and invalid input.
- **Boundaries:** the boundary cases check both "include the start" and "exclude the end."
- **Single day:** this test was added while investigating the same-day draft question, to show that the server handles single-day ranges correctly. The real cause was that the draft's last-updated date fell on a different day.
- **Title search:** it has its own test because it goes through a separate endpoint and schema.
- All date-related tests [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] in WSL against the real database.

Most of the 460 lines are routine. A reviewer can spend most of their time on about 60 lines across three files, then skim the rest.

## Focus here

**1. The time zone conversion in [Search.tsx](app/scenes/Search/Search.tsx), `toDateRangeParams()` (about 20 lines)**

This is the core logic of the feature and has **no automated test**. The server tests send timestamps that are already converted, so nothing checks that the browser converts correctly. Questions to ask:
- Does `parseISODate` give local midnight? (It does. It's an existing Outline helper built on date-fns `parseISO`.)
- Is adding one day to the end date right across a daylight-saving change? `addDays` works in calendar days, so yes. I checked New York in March and June by hand.
- Is it OK that a shared link is read in each viewer's time zone? That was a deliberate choice, but the reviewer should agree with it.
- When both a preset and a range are in the URL, the preset wins. Is that the right call?

**2. The query conditions in [PostgresSearchProvider.ts](plugins/search-postgres/server/PostgresSearchProvider.ts), `buildWhere()` (16 lines)**

This is the security-sensitive part, because user input reaches the database here. Check that:
- Both dates are [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]ed as bound values, not `sequelize.literal`.
- The new conditions are added to `where[Op.and]` (must all match) and not `where[Op.or]` (any can match), which would quietly widen the results.
- `buildWhere()` really is shared by all three search methods, so no path is missed.

**3. The validation in [schema.ts](server/routes/api/documents/schema.ts), `withDateRangeValidation` and the two new fields (about 40 lines)**

Ignore the 24 lines of re-indentation in the same diff. One weak spot I'd point out myself: **`z.coerce.date()` is lenient.**
- **Loose input:** it accepts anything JavaScript's `new Date()` can read, such as `"March 1"`, `"2025"` or a number.
- **`null`:** `new Date(null)` is a valid date in **1970**, so `{"dateFrom": null}` [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]es as Jan 1, 1970 instead of being rejected.

The rest of the codebase uses the same pattern, so it's consistent, but a stricter `z.iso.datetime()` would be safer. That's a fair point for the reviewer to raise.

## Check the behavior in [DateFilter.tsx](app/scenes/Search/components/DateFilter.tsx)

It's the largest file, but about 40 lines are styling. Look at the behavior:
- **`showRange` local state:** it's set from the URL only once, when the component first renders. If the URL changes some other way (a link, or back/forward), the inputs can stay visible or stay hidden when they shouldn't. Worth a look or a quick manual test.
- **A search runs on every input change.** Typing a date can trigger several searches. There's no debounce yet.
- **`handleSelect` for "Custom range":** if a range already exists, it deliberately leaves the URL alone. Otherwise it clears the preset. Make sure that's the expected behavior.
- **Drafts page:** the optional callback hides "Custom range" there. Confirm Drafts is unchanged.
